title: POC ephemeral dataflows and DPA addendum notes
content:
Overview:
This is a working note from the Solutions Engineering workshop with AcmeCorp (POC ID: ACME-POC-7). Focus: how we can offer a short-lived, privacy-friendly POC environment for their assistant proof-of-concept while keeping contractual comfort around data retention and a DPA addendum. Not a legal doc — draft language snippets included for review by Legal (Priya).

Goals for the POC:
- Enable interactive chat + fine-tune-ish prompt set evaluation without long-term storage of customer prompts or outputs.
- Allow customer to send sample PII during testing under controlled conditions (masked/consented) and demonstrate Redwood Private options.
- Provide audit logs for troubleshooting while minimizing retained content.
- Propose DPA addendum language that allows ephemeral debugging traces for N days and aggregated metrics longer-term.

Current design choices (options to present to customer):
1) Ephemeral sandbox (recommended for early POC):
   - Request store: disabled by default. No persistent request/response content kept in hosted logs.
   - KV cache / prefix cache: stored in memory only, zero-disk snapshot. Restart clears cache.
   - Debug traces: optional, kept for 72 hours (rotated). Stored encrypted with customer-specific key.
   - Audit events: token-level counters, error codes, latency metrics stored for 180 days (no content).

2) Dedicated short-retention (for higher fidelity troubleshooting):
   - Request store: stored for 7 calendar days then automatically purged. Retention configurable per contract up to 30 days.
   - Snapshotting: explicit snapshot endpoints available to SE team. Snapshots flagged and require customer sign-off for transfer.

3) Private deployment (on-customer infra):
   - Full control to customer. Redwood provides config templates: default retention=0, optional local audit stream.
   - Key management via customer KMS recommended.

Suggested DPA addendum clauses (draft language for Legal):
- Ephemeral Data Handling: "For the duration of the POC, Provider (Redwood) will retain Customer request/response content only as expressly configured in the Statement of Work. By default, request/response content will not be persisted to disk and will be retained only in volatile memory. If Customer elects temporary persistence for debugging, such content will be retained for a maximum of 7 days unless otherwise agreed in writing."

- Debug Traces and Access: "Provider may collect debug traces containing metadata and truncated request/response excerpts strictly for troubleshooting. Debug traces will be retained no longer than 72 hours and will be encrypted at rest. Access to debug traces is limited to authorized Provider personnel listed in Annex A and requires explicit Customer approval for any export."

- Aggregated Metrics: "Provider may retain aggregated, de-identified metrics (e.g., token counts, latency histograms, error rates) for operational analysis and product improvement for up to 24 months. Aggregated metrics will not contain Customer-identifying content or user-generated text."

- Incident Response / Legal Holds: "In the event of a lawful request or security incident, Provider may preserve relevant data beyond stated retention to the extent required by law or to investigate a security incident, provided Customer is notified within a reasonable timeframe unless prohibited by law."

POC-specific operational checklist (action items):
- [ ] Decide default retention model with AcmeCorp (ephemeral vs 7-day). Owner: Eleanor. Due: 2024-10-18.
- [ ] Legal review of DPA snippets and debug access gating. Owner: Priya. Due: 2024-10-21.
- [ ] Prepare Redwood Private template with KMS integration sample. Owner: Ravi. Due: 2024-10-25.
- [ ] Add seeding script to sanitize sample dataset (remove SSNs, replace names) and include in POC repo. Owner: Sofia. Due: 2024-10-20.
- [ ] Add Confluence runbook for rotating ephemeral keys and deleting debug traces. Owner: SE team. Due: 2024-10-22.

Open questions / risks raised in workshop:
- Customer insisted on ability to export a transcript for internal QA after 30 days. This conflicts with ephemeral-by-default posture. Options: allow export snapshot at time of export + sign-off + stored under customer-managed KMS.
- Does Legal want explicit SLA around guaranteed purge (proof of deletion)? Tech can provide purge logs and a signed confirmation but not secure deletion proof on SSDs for hosted environments.
- Are we comfortable with 72-hour debug trace window for all customers? Some customers want 24h max. Consider making this configurable per POC.

Technical notes / how-to for SEs:
- Toggle flags in POC config: request_persistence: [none|temporary|7d], debug_traces: [off|72h|24h], audit_aggregation: [enabled|disabled].
- For hosted POC: set request_persistence=none, debug_traces=off initially. Enable debug_traces=72h only under triage and record explicit customer approval via ticket (JIRA SE-4123).
- For Private POC: recommend setting up a vault-backed HSM key and storing debug traces in an encrypted bucket owned by the customer. Provide terraform snippets in repo.

Customer-facing options to present (short list to include in proposal):
1) Ephemeral: zero-rest persistence, 24–72h debug traces opt-in, aggregated metrics retained 24 months.
2) Short-term store: 7-day retention of request/response for debugging, snapshot export allowed with customer KMS.
3) Private full-control: everything stored on customer infra; Redwood provides templates and support.

Draft email blurb to send with proposal:
"Hi [Customer],
Attached is our recommended POC data handling approach. We recommend starting with an ephemeral sandbox (no persistent request storage) and enabling temporary debug traces only when needed. If you need a transcript export for QA, we can arrange an on-demand snapshot stored under your KMS with signed retention terms. Please review and let us know which option you prefer — we can update the SOW and DPA addendum language accordingly.

Best,
Eleanor (SE)"

Appendix: small sample SOW excerpt for retention section:
"Retention: During the POC, Provider will by default not persist request or response content to disk. Customer may opt-in to temporary persistence for troubleshooting; any temporary persistence will be retained for a maximum of 7 days unless Customer requests earlier deletion. Provider will record deletion activity in an audit log and make that log available to Customer on request."

Quick references from workshop:
- Slack thread: #acmecorp-poc (link posted in JIRA SE-4123)
- Confluence runbook draft: confluence:sec-poc-ephemeral-2024
- SE demo repo: github.com/redwood-inference/se-poc-templates (see /ephemeral-configs)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep legal language tight around "retention" vs "access" — customers care about copies held by Provider even if encrypted.
- Need an internal checklist for the debug approval flow (customer sign-off written + JIRA ticket, SE leads, legal notified).
- Explore adding an automated proof-of-purge artifact (signed timestamped manifest) to increase customer trust.

End of notes.
